No Apple Developer ID, code-signing certificate or developer account is needed on any platform. Setup then asks, one question at a time: Control this computer. Optimus does nothing until you say yes. While it's off, every tool except permissions replies that Optimus is off. How you talk to Optimus. Both (recommended), Chat only, or Listening. Talk key. Default ctrl+alt+m (Control+Option+M on a Mac). Asked only in Listening or Both. Who listens and speaks? Asked only when Mercury has no OpenAI provider. With one, OpenAI Realtime is used and this step is skipped. Change any of it later in /plugins optimus. Optimus has no account to link.

macOS charges Accessibility and Screen Recording to the app that started a process, so if Optimus ran under your terminal, the grant would cover every script that terminal runs. Instead, Optimus builds its own Optimus.app in the plugin's data folder and signs it with a certificate made on your Mac ("Mercury Optimus (local)"). No Apple account is involved, your login keychain isn't touched, and there's no password prompt. On first use it asks for these, in System Settings → Privacy & Security: Permission Why Accessibility Moving the mouse, typing, and the talk key Screen Recording Seeing the screen Microphone Listening mode only, asked once Turn on Optimus under each one. If Screen Recording asks to quit and reopen, Optimus restarts by itself the next time it's used. Because the certificate stays the same across updates, the permissions survive plugin updates. macOS asks you to confirm Screen Recording again about once a month. To check at any time, ask Mercury to check Optimus's permissions (the permissions tool). It reports each one and, when asked to fix them, shows the system prompts and opens the right Settings page.
Nothing to grant. Optimus can't control windows that run as administrator, such as Task Manager and installers.

On X11 nothing to grant. On Wayland, see the limits in Platform support. Optimus also starts on servers and minimal installs that lack ALSA or the X11 libraries: the package carries its own copies and uses them only when your system has none. Seeing and using the screen still needs a running X11 or Wayland session, and voice needs a sound device. Pasting uses xclip on X11 and wl-copy on Wayland, so install the one for your session if you want the paste fallback.

Chat. Ask Mercury in any chat (terminal, dashboard, Telegram, WhatsApp) to use the screen. Mercury takes a look, acts, and looks again to check. Listening. Press the talk key. You hear a rising chime, then talk. Mercury answers out loud while it works on your screen and says each step as it happens ("Opening Gmail", "Typing your post"). From a chat you can also say "let's talk" and Mercury starts listening for you (the listen tool). The How you talk to Optimus setting decides which of these you get: Mode (mode) What it does both (default) Chat, plus a key to talk out loud chat Type to Mercury as usual. No talk key, no microphone. voice Press a key, talk, and hear Mercury answer In a listening session, links, lists and other details aren't read out. They go to your Mercury chat. A file Mercury makes during a session is shown in Finder or Explorer.

Default ctrl+alt+m (Control+Option+M on a Mac). What a press does depends on the moment: When Pressing the talk key Not listening Starts listening (rising chime) Optimus is working Stops everything. Every action halts and the session stays open, so you can keep talking. Mercury is speaking Interrupts it All quiet Ends the session (falling chime) Muted Unmutes A key is modifiers plus one key: a letter, a digit, space, enter, tab, esc or f1 to f12. Modifiers are ctrl, alt (Option on a Mac), shift and cmd (Command on a Mac, Win on Windows). A plain letter isn't allowed, because it would fire while you type: add ctrl, alt or cmd, or use an F key. Examples: ctrl+alt+m, ctrl+shift+space, f9.

Default ctrl+alt+shift+m (Control+Option+Shift+M on a Mac). Muting stops listening but not working: Mercury keeps doing the task and still talks, and nothing you say is sent anywhere. Saying "mute" also mutes. Press the mute key again, or the talk key, to unmute. A session doesn't time out while muted.

Say "stop" (also "cancel", "halt", "abort", "enough", "never mind", "ruko", "bas") and every screen action halts at once, along with the Mercury task the session started. Mercury says "Stopped." and waits. New screen actions are refused for a few seconds while the task is cancelled; your next request lifts the stop. Say "bye" ("goodbye", "that's all", "stop listening") to stop everything and end the session.

Silence. When you haven't spoken for 60 seconds and Mercury isn't working on anything, the mic closes by itself, so it never streams (and costs) for nothing. Change it with Stop listening after silence; 0 keeps listening until you press the key or say bye. Length. A session ends after 30 minutes at most (Longest listening session).
documents.s: When a session ends by itself

documents.t: With speakers, Optimus mutes the mic while Mercury talks so it doesn't hear itself; press the talk key to interrupt. With headphones, turn on Headphones in /plugins optimus → 🎙 Voice to interrupt just by talking.

While Mercury searches or works and nobody is talking, a quiet wooden tick-tock plays, so you know it's still going. It's well below speech level and never mutes the mic, so you can say "stop" over it. Turn it off with Tick-tock while working.

"Mercury is driving." While Optimus moves the mouse, a ring follows the pointer with the label ☿ Mercury · Optimus is driving, and fades a moment after the last action. On macOS and Windows it's excluded from screen capture; on Linux X11 it's hidden while a screenshot is taken, so it never appears in Optimus's own screenshots. Wayland doesn't allow it. Turn it off with "Mercury is driving" ring by the pointer. Status bar. The terminal UI's status bar shows when Optimus is listening (🎙), working (🖱) or muted (🔇). Pace. In Natural pace the pointer glides along a gentle curve, scrolling arrives in small steps, and text is typed key by key at an uneven human rhythm. Typing (not pasting) means it works in every editor. Fast does the same moves with less waiting.

An action reaching the screen doesn't mean it worked. Optimus reports each step as Sent, not done, and returns a fresh screenshot. Mercury is told to look again and check the exact result (the post is published, the file is saved) before it says a task is done. Every step that failed or was stopped is recorded. In a listening session, Mercury's answer is checked against that record before you hear it: if steps failed, the voice is told which ones and not to call the task done unless Mercury confirmed it on the screen. With your own Mercury model as the voice, an answer that doesn't admit the failure starts with "Heads up, some steps didn't work."

Off until you allow it. Nothing works until you turn on Control this computer. Approvals. Ordinary, reversible steps (clicking, typing, scrolling) run straight away. The step that commits something (submit a form, send a message or email, post, pay or buy, delete, install, change a setting) goes through act_consequential, which needs your approval like any other Mercury action. In a listening session the approval is asked out loud and you answer by voice. Move the mouse to take over. If you move the mouse while Optimus is working, it stops at the next step and hands control back. No secrets. Optimus is told never to type passwords, card numbers or 2FA codes. It asks you to do that part. Stop. The talk key while it's working, or saying "stop", halts everything at once. No anti-cheat games. Mercury declines to play or automate games that use anti-cheat (Valorant, Fortnite, Call of Duty, Counter-Strike 2, or anything running Vanguard, Easy Anti-Cheat or BattlEye). Automated input breaks those games' rules and can get your account banned. Single-player and offline games without anti-cheat are fine. This is an instruction Mercury follows, not a technical block.

Screenshots are taken only when Mercury looks at the screen or acts on it, never in the background. Each is the display the mouse is on, scaled to fit 1280×800. They go to your model for that step only, and are kept out of chat history, logs and memory. If your model can't take images, the screenshot is left out and Mercury is told so. The microphone is open only during a listening session. It closes on silence, when you press the key or say bye, and at the session limit. While muted, nothing is sent. In Chat only mode the microphone is never used. Voice audio goes only to the voice engine you chose.

Pick who listens and speaks in /plugins optimus → 🎙 Voice. The options, settings and defaults are the same as for WhatsApp calls: OpenAI Realtime (default, uses your Mercury OpenAI provider), Gemini Live, Grok Voice (your Mercury Grok provider), ElevenLabs Realtime (experimental), Azure OpenAI Realtime, Qwen-Omni Realtime, or your own Mercury model with a speech-to-text and a text-to-speech provider. Voice keys are shared with the WhatsApp plugin: a key added for one works for the other.

Open /plugins optimus. Settings are listed on the menu with their current values. Voice settings appear only in Listening or Both mode. Setting Key Default What it does Control this computer allowControl off On: Optimus can see your screen and use the mouse and keyboard. Off: it does nothing. How you talk to Optimus mode both both, chat or voice (see above). How Optimus moves and types pace natural natural (like a person) or fast (same moves, less waiting). "Mercury is driving" ring by the pointer showOverlay on The ring and label while Optimus moves the mouse. Talk key hotkey ctrl+alt+m Start and stop listening, interrupt, or stop work. Mute key muteHotkey ctrl+alt+shift+m Stop listening while Mercury keeps working. Under 🎙 Voice: Setting Key Default What it does Who listens and speaks? voiceEngine openai The voice engine. Engine-specific keys, models and voices follow, as for WhatsApp. Headphones bargeIn off On: interrupt just by talking. Off: the mic waits while Mercury talks. Tick-tock while working thinkingSound on The soft tick-tock while Mercury searches or works. Stop listening after silence (seconds) idleStopSeconds 60 0 keeps listening until you press the key or say bye. Longest listening session (minutes) maxSessionMinutes 30 A session ends by itself after this long. The engine settings (voiceModel, voice, geminiKey, geminiModel, geminiVoice, grokModel, grokVoice, elevenlabsKey, elevenlabsModel, elevenlabsVoice, azureKey, azureEndpoint, azureDeployment, qwenKey, qwenEndpoint, qwenModel, qwenVoice, sttProvider, sttLanguage, ttsProvider, ttsVoice and the provider keys) have the same names and defaults as in the WhatsApp plugin.

These are what Mercury uses. You don't call them yourself. Tool What it does Approval optimus__look Screenshot of the display the mouse is on (or display N), with an optional zoom No optimus__act Click, double-click, right-click, drag, draw, type, paste, key combos, scroll, wait; returns a fresh screenshot No optimus__act_consequential The same, for the step that submits, sends, pays, deletes, installs or changes a setting Yes optimus__open Open an app by name, a URL, or a file or folder No optimus__windows List open windows, front first No optimus__permissions Check (and request) the OS permissions No optimus__listen Start a listening session from chat No

"Optimus is off". Turn on Control this computer in /plugins optimus. "Can't take a screenshot" or "can't control the mouse and keyboard" on macOS. Open System Settings → Privacy & Security and turn on Optimus under Screen Recording and Accessibility. Or ask Mercury to check Optimus's permissions; it opens the right page. The talk key does nothing. Open /plugins optimus: the menu shows whether the talk key is working, or why not (for example a key it couldn't parse). Make sure the mode is Listening or Both. On macOS the key needs Accessibility. On Wayland, the key only works while an XWayland app has focus; use chat, or ask Mercury to start listening. "Optimus can't listen yet: voice calls need an OpenAI provider". The default engine uses Mercury's OpenAI provider. Add your OpenAI key once in the dashboard (Providers) or with mercury doctor, or pick another engine in /plugins optimus → 🎙 Voice. It stops halfway with "you moved the mouse". That's the takeover check. Keep your hands off the mouse while Optimus is working, or take over on purpose and ask it to carry on. It can't click in Task Manager or an installer (Windows). Windows blocks input to apps running as administrator. Mercury keeps hearing itself. Use headphones and turn on Headphones, or leave it off so the mic waits while Mercury talks.

/plugins disable optimus turns it off and keeps its settings. /plugins uninstall optimus removes it; add --purge to delete its data too (on macOS, including Optimus.app and its local certificate). You can then remove Optimus from the macOS privacy lists. See also: Plugins, WhatsApp, Writing plugins.

Mercury connects to Signal via a signal-cli bridge, providing an end-to-end encrypted conversational interface with support for group chats and private DMs, pairing-code access control, and real-time task progress.

Important: Platform and dependency requirements Signal integration has specific requirements that must be met before it will work: Operating system: Linux (x64 or ARM64) or macOS (Apple Silicon or Intel). Windows is not supported — signal-cli native binaries are not available for Windows. signal-cli: Mercury automatically downloads and manages signal-cli v0.14.5. On Linux, native binaries are available for x64 and ARM64. On macOS (or on Linux without native binaries), Mercury falls back to the Java-based signal-cli which requires Java 17+ (java on your PATH). Phone number: You need a real phone number capable of receiving SMS or calls for Signal verification during registration. This number will be your Mercury bot's Signal identity. Network access: Signal servers must be reachable from your machine. If you're behind a firewall, ensure signal-cli can reach https://chat.signal.org and https://storage.signal.org. Storage: Approximately 50 MB for the signal-cli binary/JAR plus data storage in ~/.mercury/signal-cli/. First-time registration On first run, Mercury will guide you through the signal-cli registration process. This involves: Registering your phone number with Signal (SMS or voice verification). Verifying the code Signal sends you. Setting a Signal profile name for the bot. This is a one-time setup — once registered, Mercury will automatically start the signal-cli daemon on subsequent launches.

Mercury's Signal integration works by running signal-cli in JSON-RPC mode as a managed subprocess. Mercury: Downloads the correct signal-cli binary for your platform (or uses the JAR if native binaries aren't available). Registers the phone number with Signal on first run (interactive CLI flow). Starts the signal-cli JSON-RPC daemon as a managed subprocess. Communicates via JSON-RPC over a local socket — no external API needed. Manages the daemon lifecycle (start, stop, health checks, auto-restart). All messages between you and Mercury travel through Signal's end-to-end encryption. Mercury never stores your Signal messages.

On macOS, Java is typically already available. On Linux, install it if you don't have it: # Ubuntu/Debian sudo apt install openjdk-17-jre # Fedora/RHEL sudo dnf install java-17-openjdk # Alpine apk add openjdk17 To verify: java -version # Should show 17 or later Skip Java on Linux with native binaries On Linux x64 and ARM64, Mercury can use signal-cli native binaries that don't require Java at all. Mercury will automatically detect and use native binaries when available. Only install Java if you're on macOS or if the native binary doesn't work on your Linux system.

Run mercury doctor and select Signal when prompted, or set these environment variables: # Required SIGNAL_ENABLED=true SIGNAL_PHONE_NUMBER=+1234567890 # Your bot's phone number (E.164 format) # Optional — "group" (default) or "private" SIGNAL_MODE=group # Optional — restrict to a specific Signal group SIGNAL_GROUP_ID= SIGNAL_GROUP_NAME=Mercury Or add them to ~/.mercury/.env.

mercury up On first launch with Signal enabled, Mercury will: Download signal-cli to ~/.mercury/signal-cli/. Start the registration flow: Signal: Registering +1234567890 with Signal... Signal: Verification code sent. Enter the code: Enter the verification code you receive via SMS or call. Set a profile name for your bot (e.g. "Mercury"). After registration is complete, Mercury will save the credentials and auto-start signal-cli on subsequent launches.

Group Mode (default)​ Create a Signal group named "Mercury" (or your configured SIGNAL_GROUP_NAME). Add your Mercury bot's phone number to the group. Mercury will automatically detect the group and start responding. Private Mode​ Set SIGNAL_MODE=private to use 1:1 DMs instead of a group. Send a message directly to the bot's phone number.

When a new user sends a message to the Mercury bot for the first time, they'll receive instructions to pair: Send /pair to the bot on Signal. The bot will respond with a pairing code. Enter the code in the CLI: mercury signal pair <code> You are now the Signal admin. Other users can request access by messaging the bot, and admins can approve them.

Mercury Signal uses an organization access model with admins and members. Role Description Can approve requests? Admin First user to pair. Can approve/reject access requests, promote/demote users. Yes Member Approved by an admin. Can send messages and receive responses. No Pending Sent /start but not yet approved. No

Command Description mercury signal list Show approved admins, members, and pending requests mercury signal approve <userId> Approve a pending request mercury signal reject <userId> Reject a pending request mercury signal remove <userId> Remove an approved admin or member mercury signal promote <userId> Promote a member to admin mercury signal demote <userId> Demote an admin to member mercury signal reset Clear all Signal access (start fresh) Phone number display In CLI output, phone numbers are redacted (e.g. +1***890) for privacy. The full numbers are stored in ~/.mercury/mercury.yaml but never displayed in logs or terminal output.

Mercury listens for messages in a Signal group named "Mercury" (configurable via SIGNAL_GROUP_NAME). This is the recommended mode because: Messages are visible to all group members (useful for team collaboration). Mercury auto-detects the group by name. You can override the group with SIGNAL_GROUP_ID for precise control.

Set SIGNAL_MODE=private for 1:1 conversations. In this mode: Mercury only responds to direct messages (not group messages). Each user gets their own conversation thread. Access control still applies — unapproved users see a pairing prompt.

Feature Description End-to-end encryption All messages use Signal's E2E encryption Group and private modes Listen in a named group or respond to DMs Pairing code onboarding Secure admin setup via CLI pairing code Auto-managed signal-cli Download, register, start, and health-check handled automatically Message deduplication Duplicate messages are filtered within a 60-second window Rate limiting Built-in busy detection prevents message flooding Long message splitting Messages over 4000 characters are split into multiple Signal messages Phone number redaction CLI output always redacts phone numbers for privacy

Variable Description Default SIGNAL_ENABLED Enable/disable Signal channel false SIGNAL_PHONE_NUMBER Bot's phone number (E.164 format, e.g. +1234567890) — SIGNAL_MODE "group" or "private" group SIGNAL_GROUP_ID Restrict to a specific Signal group (hex ID). Leave empty for auto-detect by name. — SIGNAL_GROUP_NAME Name of the Signal group to auto-detect Mercury

signal-cli won't start On macOS: Make sure Java 17+ is installed and java is on your PATH. On Linux: Try the native binary first. If it fails, install Java 17+ and Mercury will fall back to the JAR. Run mercury logs for detailed error output. Registration fails Make sure your phone number is in E.164 format (e.g. +1234567890). Ensure your phone number can receive SMS or calls from Signal. If you've previously registered this number, you may need to re-register: mercury signal unregister then start again. Bot doesn't respond in the group Verify the group name matches SIGNAL_GROUP_NAME (default: "Mercury"). Try setting SIGNAL_GROUP_ID directly to the group's hex ID (you can find it in mercury logs). Make sure the bot's phone number has been added to the group. "Unpaired" response New users need to send /pair and then complete the CLI pairing flow. If you've lost admin access, run mercury signal reset to start fresh. signal-cli crashes repeatedly Check ~/.mercury/signal-cli/ for the data directory. Corrupted data can cause crashes. Try removing the data directory and re-registering: Warning: this will delete your Signal identity and you'll need to re-register. Check mercury logs for the specific error. Windows is not supported Signal integration requires signal-cli which does not have Windows native binaries. Consider using Docker with a Linux container if you need Signal on a Windows host.

Mercury connects to Slack as a Socket Mode bot, providing a real-time conversational interface with slash commands, streaming responses, and an organization-style access model with pairing codes and admin controls.

A Slack workspace where you can install apps. A Slack App with Bot Token (xoxb-) and App-Level Token (xapp-). Node.js 18 or later (for the @slack/bolt v4 dependency). Socket Mode required Mercury uses Socket Mode, which means it connects to Slack via WebSocket — no public endpoint or HTTPS certificate is needed. Your Slack app must have Socket Mode enabled and an App-Level Token with connections:write scope.
Go to api.slack.com/apps and click Create New App → From scratch. Give it a name (e.g. "Mercury") and select your workspace. Click Create App.

In your app's settings, navigate to Socket Mode in the left sidebar. Toggle Enable Socket Mode on. Enter a token name (e.g. "mercury-socket") and click Generate. Copy the xapp- token — you'll need this as SLACK_APP_TOKEN.
documents.s: Step 2: Enable Socket Mode and Get App-Level Token

documents.t: Navigate to OAuth & Permissions in the left sidebar. Under Bot Token Scopes, add these scopes: chat:write — send messages chat:write.public — send messages in channels the bot hasn't joined chat:write.customize — customize message appearance (for streaming edits) channels:history — read channel messages groups:history — read private channel messages im:history — read direct messages im:write — send direct messages files:write — upload files commands — handle slash commands app_mentions:read — respond to @mentions Click Install App to Workspace (or reinstall if already installed). Copy the Bot User OAuth Token (xoxb-) — this is SLACK_BOT_TOKEN.

Navigate to Event Subscriptions in the left sidebar. Toggle Enable Events on. Under Subscribe to bot events, add: message.channels — receive messages in public channels message.groups — receive messages in private channels message.im — receive direct messages app_mention — respond when @mentioned Click Save Changes.
Navigate to Interactivity & Shortcuts in the left sidebar. Toggle Interactivity on. Click Save Changes.

Navigate to Slash Commands in the left sidebar. Click Create New Command. Fill in: Command: /mercury Request URL: (leave default — Socket Mode handles this) Short description: Interact with Mercury Agent Usage hint: start | status | help Click Save.
Navigate to App Home in the left sidebar. Check Allow users to send Slash commands and messages from the messages tab. Click Save.
In Slack, go to the channel where you want Mercury to respond and type: /invite @Mercury
documents.s: Step 8: Invite the Bot to a Channel

documents.t: Run mercury doctor and select Slack when prompted, or set these environment variables: # Required SLACK_ENABLED=true SLACK_BOT_TOKEN=xoxb-your-bot-token SLACK_APP_TOKEN=xapp-your-app-token # Optional — restrict to a specific channel SLACK_CHANNEL_ID= # Optional — workspace/team ID SLACK_TEAM_ID= # Optional — enable streaming (edit-in-place) responses (default: true) SLACK_STREAMING=true Or add them to ~/.mercury/.env.

Start Mercury: mercury up In Slack, DM the bot or mention it in a channel with: /mercury start Mercury will display a pairing code. Enter it in the CLI: mercury slack pair <code> You are now the Slack admin. Other users can request access, and you can approve them from the CLI.

Mercury Slack uses an organization access model with admins and members. Role Description Can approve requests? Admin First user to pair. Can approve/reject access requests, promote/demote users. Yes Member Approved by an admin. Can send messages and receive responses. No Pending Sent /mercury start but not yet approved. No

Command Description mercury slack list Show approved admins, members, and pending requests mercury slack approve <userId> Approve a pending request by Slack user ID mercury slack reject <userId> Reject a pending request mercury slack remove <userId> Remove an approved admin or member mercury slack promote <userId> Promote a member to admin mercury slack demote <userId> Demote an admin to member mercury slack reset Clear all Slack access (start fresh)

Feature Description Socket Mode No public endpoint needed — connects via WebSocket Streaming responses Messages are edited in place as tokens arrive Slash commands /mercury for start, status, help, and more Channel + DM support Works in channels (when @mentioned) and direct messages Organization access Admin/member roles with pairing-code onboarding App mentions Respond when @mentioned in channels File handling Send and receive file attachments

Variable Description Default SLACK_ENABLED Enable/disable Slack channel false SLACK_BOT_TOKEN Bot User OAuth Token (xoxb-) — SLACK_APP_TOKEN App-Level Token for Socket Mode (xapp-) — SLACK_CHANNEL_ID Restrict to a specific channel. Leave empty for all channels. — SLACK_TEAM_ID Workspace/Team ID (optional) — SLACK_STREAMING Enable real-time streaming (edit-in-place) true

Bot doesn't respond to messages Make sure SLACK_ENABLED=true and both SLACK_BOT_TOKEN and SLACK_APP_TOKEN are set. Verify the bot token starts with xoxb- and the app token starts with xapp-. Check that event subscriptions include message.channels, message.groups, message.im, and app_mention. Run mercury logs to check for connection errors. Socket Mode connection failures Ensure Socket Mode is enabled in your Slack App settings. Verify the App-Level Token has the connections:write scope. If you're behind a firewall, ensure WebSocket connections to wss://slack.com are allowed. Bot doesn't respond in channels Make sure you've invited the bot to the channel: /invite @Mercury Check that channels:history and chat:write.public scopes are enabled. Slash commands not working Make sure Interactivity is enabled in your Slack App settings. Verify the /mercury slash command is configured correctly. Streaming not working Ensure SLACK_STREAMING=true (default). Slack rate-limits message edits — Mercury handles this automatically by falling back to new messages when rate-limited.

Mercury connects to your Spotify account natively — control playback, search music, manage playlists, and DJ on your devices through natural conversation. No browser tabs, no app switching. Just say "play some chill music" and Mercury handles the rest. Spotify Premium Read-only features (search, top tracks, playlists, now playing) work on free Spotify accounts. Playback control (play, pause, skip, volume, shuffle, repeat, queue) requires a Spotify Premium subscription — this is a Spotify API limitation, not a Mercury restriction.

Go to developer.spotify.com/dashboard Log in with your Spotify account Click "Create app" Fill in: App name: Mercury (or anything you like) App description: Mercury Agent Spotify Integration Redirect URI: http://127.0.0.1:8888/callback — this must match exactly Click Save On the app's settings page, copy the Client ID and Client Secret Development Mode When your Spotify Developer app is in development mode (the default), you can grant access to up to 25 users. Go to your app's settings → User Management → add the Spotify email addresses of anyone who should be able to connect. This is perfect for personal use or small teams. If you need more than 25 users, you'll need to request extended quota from Spotify.
documents.s: Step 1: Create a Spotify Developer App

documents.t: Run mercury doctor (or mercury setup for first-time setup): mercury doctor When prompted for Spotify, choose Yes and enter: Spotify Client ID — paste the Client ID from Step 1 Spotify Client Secret — paste the Client Secret from Step 1 Press Enter on any other field to keep its current value. After setup, you'll see: Spotify: not connected — run /spotify auth to link your account

Start Mercury and run: /spotify auth Choose your authorization method: Method When to use Open browser (recommended) When Mercury is running locally on your machine Paste authorization code When browser auto-open fails, or via SSH For SSH or Telegram, Mercury will give you the auth URL. Open it on any device with a browser, then paste the code parameter from the redirect URL: /spotify code <paste-your-code-here> After successful auth, Mercury shows: Spotify: connected as YourName

Command Description /spotify Show connection status, account name, plan, and active device /spotify auth Start OAuth flow (browser or manual code) /spotify code <code> Complete auth with a pasted authorization code /spotify logout Disconnect Spotify and clear saved tokens /spotify player Interactive player with arrow-key controls (CLI only) /spotify devices List available Spotify devices /spotify device <id> Set active device /spotify now Show what is currently playing
These are the tools Mercury uses when you talk about music:

Tool What it does spotify_search Search tracks, artists, albums, playlists spotify_now_playing Show what's currently playing spotify_devices List available Spotify devices spotify_top_tracks Get your top tracks (time_range: short/medium/long term) spotify_playlists Get your playlists spotify_like Save a track to your library

Tool What it does spotify_play Play a track, album, or playlist on a device spotify_pause Pause playback spotify_next Skip to next track spotify_previous Skip to previous track spotify_volume Set volume (0-100) spotify_shuffle Toggle shuffle on/off spotify_repeat Set repeat mode (off, track, context) spotify_queue Add a track to the playback queue

Just talk to Mercury naturally about music: You say Mercury does "play some chill music" Searches "lo-fi chill", picks tracks, plays on your device "what are my top tracks?" Calls spotify_top_tracks, shows results "skip this song" Calls spotify_next "pause" Calls spotify_pause "play my playlist Road Trip" Searches your playlists, plays the match "set volume to 50" Calls spotify_volume(50) "what's playing?" Calls spotify_now_playing, shows artist — track + progress bar "add this to my queue" Calls spotify_queue with current track "shuffle on" Calls spotify_shuffle(true)

The /spotify player command launches an interactive arrow-key player in your terminal: ▶ Play/Pause ◀ Previous ▶▶ Next 🔊 Volume 🔀 Shuffle 🔁 Repeat 🔍 Search 📋 Queue ✕ Exit Every action shows real-time feedback with track info and a progress bar.

Mercury's Spotify flow supports a practical DJ mode pattern in conversation and in the CLI player: Queue songs while current playback continues Skip/recover quickly with next/previous controls Adjust energy with volume/shuffle/repeat in-session Keep steering by prompts like: "Queue 3 upbeat tracks" "Skip this and play something calmer" "Keep this vibe for the next 20 minutes" Use /spotify player for hands-on control, or use natural-language prompts to keep the set moving.
Inside the Spotify player (CLI): N → next track P → previous track + / - → volume up/down by 10% Z → refresh now playing Esc → exit player

Mercury supports inline album art as a progressive enhancement (text UI remains the default). Enable with: MERCURY_SPOTIFY_ART=1 Currently rendered only in local iTerm sessions Automatically falls back to text-only view in SSH/mobile/light terminals

Spotify plays on your devices — phone, desktop, TV, speaker. Mercury never plays audio locally. Before playing, Mercury checks what devices are available: /spotify devices If no device is active, Mercury will tell you to open Spotify on a device first. You can set a default device: /spotify device <device-id> The device ID persists across sessions — Mercury remembers your preferred device.

Mercury stores your Spotify tokens in ~/.mercury/mercury.yaml: Access token — short-lived, auto-refreshed Refresh token — long-lived, used to get new access tokens Account info — display name, user ID, plan (Premium/Free) Tokens refresh automatically before they expire. If the refresh token itself expires (rare), run /spotify auth again.
/spotify logout This clears all tokens and account info. Run /spotify auth to reconnect later.

Client credentials Your Spotify Client ID and Client Secret are stored in ~/.mercury/mercury.yaml. They are only used to authenticate with Spotify's API from your machine — never shared externally. Treat this file like any other credential. Your access and refresh tokens are also stored locally. Mercury never sends them anywhere except Spotify's API endpoints.

Issue Solution "Spotify Premium is required" error You need Premium for playback control. Read-only features still work on free accounts. 403 errors on play/pause/skip Your account is on Spotify's free tier. Playback APIs are Premium-only. "No active device" Open Spotify on your phone/computer, play any song, then try again. Browser doesn't open for auth Use the manual code flow: /spotify auth → choose "Paste code" Token expired after long idle Run /spotify auth to get fresh tokens Account name not showing Run /spotify and Mercury will fetch it live from Spotify's API

Mercury isn't just a chatbot — it's an orchestrator. It can spawn parallel AI agents to handle tasks concurrently while continuing the conversation. This is sub-agent mode, and it changes how Mercury works fundamentally.

Traditional AI agents are single-threaded: one context window, one task at a time. If you ask Mercury to "research this topic, write the code, and review the result," it does them sequentially — each step blocks the next. Sub-agents break this bottleneck: Parallel execution — Multiple tasks run simultaneously across isolated context windows LLM-driven delegation — Mercury itself decides when to delegate based on task complexity Non-blocking — You can keep chatting with Mercury while sub-agents work in the background File locks — Reader-writer locks prevent concurrent write conflicts between agents Resource-aware — Max concurrent agents is auto-detected from your system's CPU and RAM

You: "Build a REST API for users and write integration tests" Mercury decides to delegate: 🤖 Multi-agent mode activated. **Agent a1** is now working on: "Build REST API endpoints for users" **Agent a2** is now working on: "Write integration tests for user endpoints" Active agents: 2/4 You can continue chatting while the agents work. Use /agents to check status. Mercury: I've delegated both tasks to parallel agents. Agent a1 is building the API and agent a2 is writing tests. They'll work independently. (you continue chatting normally) 🔄 Agent a1: Using: read_file, create_file 🔄 Agent a2: Using: list_dir, read_file ✅ **Agent a1** completed (12.3s): "REST API built with 5 endpoints" ✅ **Agent a2** completed (18.7s): "12 integration tests passing" Both agents are done. Want me to review the results together?

Command Description /agents List all sub-agents (running and completed) /agents stop <id|all> Stop a sub-agent or all sub-agents /agents pause <id> Pause a running sub-agent /agents resume <id> Resume a paused sub-agent /agents config Show sub-agent resource allocation (max concurrent, mode) /agents set max <n> Set max concurrent sub-agents /code agent <task> Delegate a coding task to a sub-agent immediately /bg: <task> Run a natural-language sub-agent task in background /bg current Move current in-flight task to a background sub-agent /bg list List shell + sub-agent background tasks /halt Emergency: halt all sub-agents and clear the task queue /stop Full stop: halt agents, clear queue, release file locks, clear task board /reset Full reset: stop all + clear conversation context (requires confirmation) /halt vs /stop vs /reset /halt stops all agents but preserves conversation context and file locks. /stop goes further — it also releases file locks and clears the task board. /reset does everything /stop does plus clears the conversation context (requires confirmation). Slash commands like /agents, /halt, /stop, /spotify, and /code work even while the main agent is busy — they're processed immediately on a fast path.

Mercury uses these tools to manage sub-agents: Tool Description delegate_task Spawn a sub-agent with a task description and optional context list_agents Show all running and completed sub-agents stop_agent Halt a specific running sub-agent by ID When Mercury decides a task is complex enough to benefit from parallel execution, it calls delegate_task. You'll see a response like: 🤖 Multi-agent mode activated. **Agent a1** is now working on: "Analyze the codebase structure for..." Active agents: 1/4 You can continue chatting while the agent works. I'll notify you when it's done. Use /agents to check status.

User message → Main Agent (orchestrator) ├─ delegate_task("research X") → Sub-Agent a1 (isolated context) ├─ delegate_task("implement Y") → Sub-Agent a2 (isolated context) └─ continues conversation → responds to user │ a1: "🔄 Using: read_file" a1: "🔄 Using: edit_file" a2: "🔄 Using: list_dir" a1: "✅ completed (8.2s)" a2: "🔄 Using: create_file" a2: "✅ completed (15.1s)" Each sub-agent: Has its own context window — the main agent's conversation doesn't pollute it Runs an independent 10-step agentic loop with the same tool access Uses the same permission system — but with auto-approve for the task's scope Reports progress via the notification channel (CLI or Telegram) Respects file locks — if a1 is writing a file, a2 waits for the lock

Mercury decides to delegate when: A task is naturally parallelizable (e.g., "research X while I code Y") The task benefits from an isolated context window (no pollution from the main conversation) A task is complex enough to warrant dedicated focus Multiple independent investigations would save time You can also ask Mercury explicitly: "Use two agents for this" or "Delegate this task."

You can keep chatting normally. Mercury processes your messages as they come in. Sub-agent progress and completion appear as notification messages in your channel: 🔄 Agent a1: Starting task... 🔄 Agent a1: Using: read_file, edit_file 🔄 Agent a2: Using: fetch_url, create_file ✅ Agent a1 completed (8.2s): "Analyzed the codebase..." 🔄 Agent a2: Using: run_command ✅ Agent a2 completed (14.5s): "Tests passing..." If you send /agents, you'll see the full status: **Sub-Agents:** 🔄 a1: Build REST API endpoints — running (Using: read_file) ⏳ a2: Write integration tests — pending Background-tracked agent tasks also appear in /bg list so shell jobs and delegated coding work share one progress surface.

Sub-agents are configured in ~/.mercury/mercury.yaml: subagents: enabled: true maxConcurrent: auto # auto-detected from CPU/RAM, or set manually (e.g., 4) mode: auto # "auto" (LLM decides) or "manual" (user controls) Environment variable overrides: Variable Description SUBAGENTS_ENABLED Enable/disable sub-agents SUBAGENTS_MAX_CONCURRENT Max number of concurrent agents SUBAGENTS_MODE auto or manual

Sub-agents pair well with Mercury's programming mode for code tasks: Command Mode Behavior /code plan Plan Analyze without writing code /code execute Execute Implement step by step /code off Off Normal conversation /code toggle — Cycle through modes /code status — Show current mode

When /code plan is active, Mercury will analyze a task and present a plan. If the plan involves parallel work, Mercury can delegate parts to sub-agents during /code execute. The ask_user tool lets Mercury present choices at decision points — on CLI this is an arrow-key menu, on Telegram it's inline buttons.
Mercury connects to Telegram via a bot token, providing a mobile-first interface with streaming, file uploads, inline approval keyboards, and real-time task progress.

Mercury uses an organization access model with admins and members. The first user becomes the admin by completing a pairing-code flow during setup. Additional users request access by sending /start, which admins can approve or reject. First-time pairing When no admins exist yet, sending /start creates a pairing code that must be entered in the CLI to complete setup. This ensures only the legitimate owner can gain initial access. Once an admin exists, new users send /start to create a pending request that admins can approve or reject. Private chats only Mercury only works in private (one-to-one) chats. Messages in groups or channels are always ignored.

Role Description Can approve requests? Admin First user to pair. Can approve/reject access requests, promote/demote users, and reset all access. Yes Member Approved by an admin. Can send messages and receive responses. No Pending Sent /start but not yet approved. Can only see their pending status. No

Command Description mercury telegram list Show approved admins, members, and pending requests mercury telegram approve <code|userId> Approve the first pairing code or a pending request by user ID mercury telegram reject <userId> Reject a pending access request mercury telegram remove <userId> Remove an approved admin or member mercury telegram promote <userId> Promote a member to admin mercury telegram demote <userId> Demote an admin to member (at least one admin must remain) mercury telegram reset Clear all Telegram access (admins, members, pending). Start fresh.

Mercury registers 15 commands in Telegram's bot menu for quick access: Command Description /start Request access to this Mercury instance /help Show Telegram-specific command reference /status Config, budget, and uptime /progress Live status for the current task /stop Stop all agents and clear queue /budget Token budget status and management /stream Toggle text streaming on/off /memory Second brain memory /permissions Switch Ask Me / Allow All mode /models List providers or switch AI model /code Programming mode (plan / execute / off) /agents List and manage sub-agents /bg Background tasks /spotify Spotify playback controls /unpair Reset all Telegram access (admin only) Telegram-specific help Running /help on Telegram shows a clean, Telegram-formatted command reference with only Telegram-relevant commands — no CLI-only features like workspace IDE or progress views.
During multi-step tasks, Mercury uses a single status card that updates in place. This keeps the chat clean — you see one message that shows what's happening, not a flood of separate updates.

Step 1 begins — Mercury creates a status card: ⚙️ Mercury working (step 1) Steps progress — The same message is edited to show the latest steps with checkmarks Step 3+ (substantial task) — The status card is pinned to the top of the chat so you can always see progress without scrolling Notices — System messages like Mercury Autopilot warnings are folded into the status card instead of creating separate messages Task completes — The status card is unpinned and deleted. The AI response and completion banner appear as fresh messages
⚙️ Mercury working (step 5) ✅ read_file · src/index.ts ✅ edit_file · src/utils.ts ✅ run_command · npm test ✅ read_file · package.json ⏳ write_file · src/config.ts…
documents.s: What the Status Card Looks Like

documents.t: During an active task, no new messages are created in the chat. Everything is consolidated into the pinned status card: Tool progress — edited in place with a rolling window of the last 5 completed steps Autopilot warnings — shown as notice lines in the status card (last 3 notices) AI responses — deferred until the task completes, then sent as a clean message Permission prompts — shown as ephemeral inline keyboard messages, deleted after you respond This means you never have to scroll up to find the progress indicator — it stays pinned at the top until the task is done.

When a substantial task finishes (3+ steps and 30+ seconds), Mercury sends a completion banner: ✅ Task complete (8 steps · 45s) ☿ claude-sonnet via anthropic · 12.4k tokens Budget: ██████████░░░░░ 67% (67.2k / 100.0k) ✓ read_file · src/index.ts ✓ edit_file · src/utils.ts ✓ run_command · npm test

At the start of each Telegram session, Mercury shows an inline keyboard to choose a permission mode: 🔒 Ask Me — Mercury asks before file writes, shell commands, and scope changes. Prompts appear as inline keyboards with Allow / Always / Deny buttons. ✅ Allow All — Auto-approve everything for this session. No interruptions. Use /permissions at any time to switch modes. Choosing "Always" on any permission prompt flips to auto-approve for the rest of the session.
Permission prompts, loop-continuation prompts, and mode-selection cards are ephemeral — they're deleted automatically after you respond (or after a 2-minute timeout). This keeps the chat clean.

Feature Description Single status card One message edited in place during multi-step tasks — no message clutter Pinned progress Status card pinned to chat top for tasks with 3+ steps Text streaming Real-time response editing with typing indicators (toggle with /stream) File uploads Photos, audio, video, and documents auto-detected and sent with the right API HTML formatting Markdown automatically converted to Telegram-compatible HTML Inline keyboards Permission and mode prompts shown as tappable buttons Ephemeral prompts Permission and mode cards auto-deleted after response Completion banners Token usage and budget stats for substantial tasks Multi-user access Organization model with admins and members Bot commands menu 15 commands registered in Telegram's bot menu for quick access

Telegram is set up during mercury doctor or initial onboarding. You need a bot token from @BotFather. Variable Description Default TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN Bot token from @BotFather — TELEGRAM_ENABLED Enable/disable Telegram channel false TELEGRAM_STREAMING Enable real-time text streaming true Type none as the bot token during mercury doctor to disable Telegram.

Mercury Web is a React single-page application that provides a visual interface for managing every part of the agent — chat, memory, tasks, code, and configuration. It runs locally at http://127.0.0.1:6174.
Enable the web dashboard using either method: Run mercury doctor and follow the prompts Set web.enabled: true in your mercury.yaml configuration

Option Default Description web.enabled false Enable or disable the web dashboard web.port 6174 Port the dashboard listens on MERCURY_PORT 6174 Environment variable override for port The server binds to 127.0.0.1 only and is not exposed to the network. The web server lifecycle is tied to the Mercury process — it stops when Mercury stops.

The dashboard is protected by username/password authentication. There is no default password. mercury setup asks you for one (at least 10 characters) or generates a strong one and shows it once. The username is mercury. Lost it? Run mercury web-reset-password. You will be redirected to /login for any unauthenticated request. After logging in, an HTTP-only session cookie is set. Sign out from Settings → Account or by closing the session in your browser. You can change your credentials from Settings → Account.

Mercury Web is a Progressive Web App. In Chrome, Edge, or Safari, look for the Install icon in the address bar (or File → Install Mercury Agent) to add it to your launcher. The PWA runs in its own window without browser chrome.
Landing page at /. Shows Mercury's current process state, active provider, daily token usage, recent activity, and quick links to other sections.

A multi-thread chat interface with SSE streaming. Thread sidebar — Lists all conversations. Click any thread to switch; the URL updates to /chat/<id> so you can bookmark or share links. New Chat button — Creates a new thread and navigates to its URL. Delete — Hover a thread (or open it) to reveal a trash icon. Confirmation dialog prevents accidents. Model switcher — Top of the chat header. Pick any configured provider; the choice is per-thread. Code Mode toggle — Switches the agent into coding mode for the active thread (file edits, shell calls allowed under your permission policy). Streaming — Assistant tokens arrive via Server-Sent Events; you can interrupt mid-stream.
View and manage background and scheduled tasks the agent has created or that you queued via Telegram or chat.
The Kanban Boards view for visually planning and executing agent work. See the Kanban Boards page for full details.
A browser-based IDE for editing project files, running terminal commands, and managing Git — all without leaving Mercury. See the Coding Workspace page for full details.

Mercury's memory and knowledge views — see the Second Brain reference. Memory (/second-brain/memory) — Browse, search, edit, promote, or prune memory items. Filter by scope (conscious, subconscious) and by tag. Persons (/second-brain/persons, /second-brain/persons/:id) — People Mercury has met, with their facts, last-seen timestamps, and relationships. Goals (/second-brain/goals) — Long-running goals with progress, sub-tasks, and linked memories. Graph (/second-brain/graph) — Force-directed graph visualization of memories, persons, and goals with their relationships.

Providers (/providers) — List configured LLM providers, their priority order, and switch the default. Permissions (/permissions) — Review and adjust the YOLO/strict permission policy for tools. Skills (/skills) — Install, list, and remove agent skills. See the Skills page. Schedules (/schedules) — Manage recurring or one-shot scheduled commands. Usage (/usage) — Per-day token usage charts. Profit Sharing (/profit-sharing) — Cooperative revenue-share settings (if enabled).

Three sections: Defaults — Default provider and daily token budget. Account — Change your username or password. Appearance — Light / Dark / System theme toggle. The agent personality is no longer editable from the web UI — modify it in mercury.yaml if you need to customise it.
Server: Hono on Node.js Frontend: React 19 + Vite + Tailwind CSS, shadcn/ui components State: Zustand for client state, SSE for streaming PWA: vite-plugin-pwa

The WhatsApp plugin lets you chat with Mercury on WhatsApp and talk to it by voice call. You call Mercury, or Mercury calls you ("call me at 9pm", "call me when it's done"). Mercury runs on a spare number as a linked device, the same way WhatsApp Web connects, so you don't need a WhatsApp Business account. It's an optional plugin, version 0.1.1, from the official plugin catalog. It needs Mercury 1.4.0 or newer. Unofficial protocol: use a spare number The plugin uses an unofficial, reverse-engineered WhatsApp protocol (whatsapp-rust). A WhatsApp update can break it, and automated use can get the number restricted or banned. Link a spare number you can afford to lose, not your main one. You chat with Mercury from your own number; Mercury runs on the spare one.

Mercury 1.4.0 or newer, on macOS (Apple silicon or Intel), Windows x64, or Linux (x64 or arm64). A spare phone number with WhatsApp installed on a phone, to link as Mercury's account. Your own WhatsApp number, to chat and call from. For voice calls, one voice engine (see Voice engines). The default uses the OpenAI provider you already set up in Mercury, so there may be nothing extra to configure. Text chat works without any of this.

In any Mercury chat: /plugins install whatsapp Or from a shell: mercury plugins install whatsapp Install shows what the plugin needs (network hosts, the secrets it may read, the Mercury providers it uses) and asks you to confirm. The plugin runs in its own process, so if it crashes, Mercury keeps running and restarts it. Mercury then walks you through setup, one question at a time, in the same chat (or in the dashboard under Configure → Plugins): Which number will you chat from? Your own number, with the country code. Only this number can talk to Mercury. What can Mercury do in your chat? General or Extended (see Access levels). Who handles your calls? Asked only when Mercury has no OpenAI provider. With one, OpenAI Realtime is used and this step is skipped. Picking an engine then asks for that engine's key and options. Link the spare number with a pairing code or a QR code (see below). Run the setup again anytime with /plugins setup whatsapp.

You can link with a pairing code or a QR code. Pairing code (works from any chat, including Telegram): Choose Pairing code in setup, or run /plugins pair whatsapp +15551234567 with the spare number. On the spare phone: WhatsApp → Settings → Linked devices → Link a device → Link with phone number instead, then type the 8-character code. The code is valid for about 3 minutes. Mercury confirms in the chat when the link is up. QR code: Dashboard: Configure → Plugins → WhatsApp → Link with QR code. The QR refreshes about every 20 seconds. Terminal: mercury plugins pair whatsapp prints a QR code. mercury plugins pair whatsapp --code +15551234567 gets a pairing code instead. On the spare phone: Linked devices → Link a device, then scan. Once it's linked, message the spare number from your own number to talk to Mercury. To check the link, open /plugins whatsapp and pick Send me a test message, or run mercury plugins test whatsapp. If WhatsApp logs the device out, Mercury tells you on another channel and how to link it again.
Use Unlink the account in /plugins whatsapp, the Unlink button in the dashboard, or: mercury plugins unlink whatsapp Then remove "Mercury" from Linked devices on the spare phone if it's still listed.

Text both ways. Long replies are split, and Markdown is converted to WhatsApp formatting. Files from Mercury arrive as attachments: images as photos, everything else as documents. Photos and PDFs you send are passed to the model along with your message, when the model in use accepts them. Text-only models are told the file is there but can't see it. Voice notes you send are transcribed with your Mercury OpenAI provider (gpt-4o-mini-transcribe, falling back to whisper-1) and reach Mercury as text. Without an OpenAI provider, Mercury tells you how to turn this on and asks you to type instead. Mercury knows it's on WhatsApp and writes like a text message: short, no tables or code blocks. Long output goes into a file it sends you. Built-in web_search (Extended access) means questions about news and current events get looked up, not guessed. Groups are ignored unless you turn on Answer in WhatsApp groups.

Access decides what Mercury may do in your WhatsApp chat. Change it anytime in /plugins whatsapp. Level What Mercury can do General (default) Chat and general knowledge only. No tools, files or personal memory. If something needs them, Mercury says so in one line. Extended Memory, files, tools and actions, as anywhere else. Anything risky still asks you first. Other numbers you add under Other numbers allowed to chat are members. They get their own level (What can those numbers do?), which is never more than yours, and they can't run admin commands such as /plugins. Members never get your private details (memory, files, contacts, accounts) unless you told Mercury to share them. Unknown numbers are ignored. Mercury only learns from calls (adds what you said to its memory) at Extended access.
When something needs your go-ahead in the chat, Mercury asks with a prompt you answer by reply: 1 yes 2 no 3 always for this chat No reply within 2 minutes counts as no.

Call the spare number from your own number and talk to Mercury. Mercury can also ring you when something matters (the call_owner tool), or at a time you set (Scheduled calls). Who can call: only the owner. Calls from anyone else, and group calls, are declined. During a call Mercury can look things up and act, using its tools, memory and files (at Extended access). While it works it keeps you posted instead of going silent. Approvals on a call: Mercury asks out loud and also posts the request in the chat. Say yes on the call, or reply 1 (yes) or 2 (no) in the chat. The first answer wins. A spoken yes only counts when your own transcribed words say yes, and it never becomes "always". No answer within 2 minutes is no. Links, photos and details: Mercury doesn't read links or long lists aloud. It sends them to the chat (the send_to_chat tool) and says so, or offers to. Photos and documents you send in the chat during a call are visible to Mercury, so you can ask about them on the call. After the call you get a message with the duration and the transcript. A missed or declined call from Mercury is followed by a written version of what it wanted. Limits: Mercury calls you at most 4 times an hour and a call lasts at most 15 minutes by default (see the settings below). Say goodbye to hang up, or just hang up. To turn off incoming calls without uninstalling, set Answer your voice calls to off. Your calls to the spare number then ring out.

The engine is who listens to you and speaks back on a call. Pick it in /plugins whatsapp → 🎙 Voice calls. Voice keys are shared: a key you add for the Optimus plugin works here too, and the other way round. Engine (voiceEngine) What it needs openai, OpenAI Realtime (default, recommended) The OpenAI provider you already set up in Mercury (dashboard → Providers, or mercury doctor). Nothing extra. gemini, Google Gemini Live A Gemini API key (from aistudio.google.com/apikey). Cheapest, has a free tier, speaks Hindi and Urdu. grok, xAI Grok Voice The Grok provider you set up in Mercury. elevenlabs, ElevenLabs Realtime (experimental) An ElevenLabs API key. azure, Azure OpenAI Realtime An Azure OpenAI key, endpoint and realtime deployment name. qwen, Alibaba Qwen-Omni Realtime A DashScope (Alibaba Model Studio) key. mercury, My own model Your Mercury model does the thinking. You pick who listens (speech to text) and who speaks (text to speech), each with its own key. When you change the engine in the menu, Mercury asks right away for what the new choice needs (its key, model, voice). Call audio goes only to the voice engine you chose. With My own model, audio goes to the speech-to-text and text-to-speech providers you picked, and the words go to your Mercury model.

Ask in any chat, or on a call: "call me at 9pm about the deploy", "call me back in 20 minutes", "call me tomorrow 8:30am". The time is worked out in code, in the computer's time zone, and Mercury confirms the exact time so a misunderstanding shows up straight away. For "call me when it's done", Mercury does the work first and then calls. You can also use commands: Command What it does /call 9pm about the deploy Schedule a call (also: in 20m, tomorrow 8:30am, tonight 8, now) /calls List scheduled calls /calls cancel 2 or /calls cancel all Cancel one by number, or all Calls can be scheduled up to 30 days ahead. If you don't pick up, Mercury tries once more 5 minutes later, then sends you a message. Scheduled calls survive restarts. A call that came due while Mercury wasn't running is placed when it's back (up to 2 hours late); after that you get a "missed" note instead. Only the owner can schedule calls.

Open /plugins whatsapp (or mercury plugins open whatsapp, or the dashboard). Settings are listed on the menu with their current values; pick one to change it. You can also set one directly with /plugins set whatsapp <key> <value>.

Setting Key Default What it does Which number will you chat from? owner (none, asked in setup) Your own number. Only it can talk to Mercury and call it. What can Mercury do in your chat? access general General (chat only) or Extended (memory, files, tools). Other numbers allowed to chat members (empty) Comma-separated numbers that may also chat. They can't run admin commands. What can those numbers do? memberAccess general General or Extended for members, never more than you. Answer in WhatsApp groups allowGroups off On: Mercury answers in groups when someone mentions it (owner and members only). Off: one-to-one chats only.

These live under 🎙 Voice calls in the menu. Engine-specific settings only appear when that engine is selected. Setting Key Default What it does Answer your voice calls answerCalls on Off: your calls to Mercury ring out. Who handles your calls? voiceEngine openai The voice engine (table above). Most calls from Mercury per hour maxCallsPerHour 4 Mercury won't ring you more often than this, so a looping task can't spam you. Longest call, in minutes maxCallMinutes 15 A call ends after this long. OpenAI voice model voiceModel gpt-realtime-2.1 Or gpt-realtime-2.1-mini, about 3x cheaper. OpenAI engine. OpenAI voice voice marin marin, cedar, alloy, ash, ballad, coral, echo, sage, shimmer, verse. OpenAI and Azure engines. Gemini API key geminiKey Gemini engine. Gemini Live model geminiModel gemini-3.8-live Gemini engine. Gemini voice geminiVoice Kore For example Kore, Puck, Charon, Aoede. Grok voice model grokModel grok-voice-latest Grok engine. Grok voice grokVoice eve eve, ara, leo, rex, sal, atlas, naksh, celeste, ursa, sirius, lumen. ElevenLabs API key elevenlabsKey ElevenLabs engine, or ElevenLabs as the listener or speaker for My own model. ElevenLabs Realtime model elevenlabsModel eleven_realtime_v1_mini Or eleven_realtime_v1_max. ElevenLabs voice elevenlabsVoice brian ElevenLabs engine. Azure OpenAI API key azureKey Azure engine. Azure endpoint azureEndpoint For example myresource.openai.azure.com. Azure realtime deployment name azureDeployment gpt-realtime-2.1 Azure engine. DashScope API key qwenKey Qwen engine. Qwen endpoint host qwenEndpoint dashscope-intl.aliyuncs.com Your workspace host, for example {workspace}.ap-southeast-1.maas.aliyuncs.com. Qwen model qwenModel qwen3.8-omni-flash-realtime Qwen engine. Qwen voice qwenVoice Tina Qwen engine. Who listens (speech to text) sttProvider deepgram My own model: deepgram (Nova-3), assemblyai (Universal-3.6 Pro), elevenlabs (Scribe v2), sarvam (Saaras, Indian languages incl. Urdu). Language you'll speak sttLanguage auto My own model: detect automatically, English, Hindi or Urdu. Who speaks (voice) ttsProvider cartesia My own model: cartesia (Sonic-3.6), elevenlabs (Flash), minimax (speech-2.8), sarvam (Bulbul), deepgram (Aura-2). Voice ID ttsVoice (empty) My own model. Empty uses the provider's default voice. Deepgram, AssemblyAI, Sarvam, Cartesia, MiniMax API keys deepgramKey, assemblyaiKey, sarvamKey, cartesiaKey, minimaxKey Asked only when you pick that provider for My own model. API keys you paste are stored with Mercury's own keys, never shown again, and readable only by plugins that declare them.

Mercury doesn't answer my messages. Check that you're messaging the spare number from the number in Which number will you chat from? (with the country code). Open /plugins whatsapp and look at Account: it should say linked. If not, pick Link the account. Run mercury doctor --plugins to see whether the plugin is running, and why it was turned off if it was. "I couldn't answer your call: voice calls need an OpenAI provider". The default engine uses Mercury's OpenAI provider. Add your OpenAI key once in the dashboard (Providers) or with mercury doctor, or pick another engine in /plugins whatsapp → 🎙 Voice calls. The menu marks the section needs setup until it's ready. Mercury says it can't listen to voice notes. Voice notes are transcribed with Mercury's OpenAI provider. Add one, or type the message. "Not calling: already called the owner 4 times in the last hour". That's the maxCallsPerHour limit. Raise it in the voice settings if you want more calls. The device was logged out. WhatsApp can log linked devices out. Link again with /plugins pair whatsapp or the dashboard. If it keeps happening, WhatsApp may be restricting the number. Something broke after a WhatsApp update. Update the plugin with /plugins update whatsapp. If the new version is worse, /plugins rollback whatsapp restores the previous one with its settings.

/plugins disable whatsapp turns it off and keeps its data and settings. /plugins uninstall whatsapp removes it; add --purge to delete its data (including the WhatsApp session) too. See also: Plugins, Optimus, Writing plugins.
Mercury has a built-in toolset it can use during conversations. These are not CLI commands — the agent decides when to call them.
